Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for his controversial YouTube interview, with manager Xabi Alonso confirming that the matter has been addressed internally. Fofana came under criticism following a two-hour interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani, which was published after Chelsea’s disappointing 4-1 defeat to Leeds United on Saturday. As reported by BBC Sport on Thursday, the 25-year-old was criticised for comments in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup shootout defeat to Liverpool. The interview was reportedly conducted without permission from the club, prompting further concerns at a difficult time for Chelsea. Speaking ahead of Friday’s Premier League meeting with Nottingham Forest, Alonso confirmed that Fofana had apologised and accepted that the interview was inappropriate. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content,” Alonso said. “We are here to take things seriously. He’s said it will not be repeated. We don’t want these kind of things and they won’t be repeated.” Alonso declined to disclose whether the club had imposed any disciplinary measures on the defender but confirmed that the issue had been handled. EPL: Fernandes laments Man Utd’s frequent managerial sackings Pochettino vows to turn Man United’s fortunes around Guardiola eyes national team job, reveals Italy offer “We have addressed that with him,” the Spaniard added. Meanwhile, interviewer Zach Nani defended Fofana following the backlash, insisting that the defender acknowledged his poor performances and expressed his determination to improve. Nani also defended Fofana’s decision to volunteer for penalty duties against Liverpool, explaining that the defender believed it was his responsibility as one of the senior players on the pitch. Fofana joined Chelsea from Leicester City in August 2022 in a £70 million deal but has struggled with injuries and inconsistent form. He has made 81 appearances for the Blues, including nine under Alonso this season. Chelsea have also struggled defensively, conceding 20 goals in 11 Premier League matches. They currently sit eighth in the table after suffering three defeats in their last four league outings. The Blues will hope to respond positively when they face Nottingham Forest on Friday as Alonso looks to improve the team’s performances and restore discipline within his squad.
